# Native accessibility target evidence

The immutable reference is Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The external collector imports the downloaded release and compares its `text_target.py` bytes against that commit before using the actual public tracker/snapshot methods. The source digest is `a916b65519d33b3401ebfee910c392560b86d5e70d6131aa3e6702394fef02c7`. The SHA-256 of `text-target-cases.json` is `8ec87285b0c01f0b97d27ccc10f6978a448f8eb66d9a9d7785ad1da451a0c1a7`.

Thirty independent released cases use a separate native GTK process with real Entry, TextView and PasswordEntry widgets. A file protocol changes only the target's own widgets and acknowledges each request; its own observer independently records text, caret, selection and change notifications. The target does not supply the client's capture decision, restoration result, insertion result or confirmation. Both clients discover their target through the real accessibility registry and resolve its actual process executable through `/proc`. Neither client receives an injected runtime or a preselected accessible node.

Cold capture is the first case: the external field is already focused before the client first initializes libatspi and registers its listener. Subsequent cases exercise normal and reversed selections, moved carets, cleared/changed selections, focus moving to an external button or the client's own real application window, retained snapshots after tracker close, empty input/insertion, multiline Unicode, explicit Command disclosure and the exact 2,000-character limit. Read-only targets keep the keyboard guard tied to the latest external focus. A real PasswordEntry is excluded without target-text queries or executable disclosure. A concealed ordinary Entry exposes a normal text role and retains the released behavior; concealment alone is not a password-role guarantee. Process exit makes restoration fail, direct editing return false and caret confirmation unavailable. A present-but-disabled status owner and an exited owner both refuse the tracker; the native check independently confirms ownership before/after the latter query so auto-activation cannot hide behind a false result.

Twenty-nine readiness-gated `dbus-monitor` processes observe the actual private accessibility bus. Delivery capture, restoration, direct mutation and caret confirmation produce zero `Text.GetText` calls. Only four Command cases read text, exactly at their captured selection bounds, including the oversized selection that is rejected before a provider can receive it. Removing selected text from a retained snapshot keeps its offsets and reads no further content. Executable identities are normalized only into an equality result against the real peer path; the synthetic target text and other results remain exact.

The first native comparison failed embedded-NUL insertion after deleting the selected range. The reference C binding sends the NUL-terminated prefix while retaining the original byte length and caller's character-based caret update. The native binding now preserves that behavior; the unchanged observation checks the target's actual final text and change count, rather than accepting a return value alone. The pre-fix failure remains under ignored `tmp/native-text-target-before-fix.log`.

The production module binds the distribution's libatspi directly. Accessible/interface/state objects retain GObject ownership, range/event values are freed as their declared boxed types, and error/string results are released even when a query fails. Proxies cannot cross Rust threads; the native callback checks its GLib thread before touching retained `Rc` data and catches unwinding at the C boundary. No focus-state borrow is held across reentrant accessibility queries. Listener userdata is owned explicitly because libatspi 2.60.6 disables its destroy callback. Closing deregisters the listener and clears the current focus while preserving the released direct-edit versus keyboard-fallback distinction.

Reference and native comparisons run sequentially on disposable Xvfb displays with separate session/accessibility buses, registry processes, XDG roots, homes and Xauthority files. `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` is removed so a delivery capture cannot query the visible compositor. GTK 4.22.4, libatspi 2.60.6 and scale 1 are the measured environment. Both clients use a real registered GtkApplication for own-focus cases; this avoids the incomplete cache advertisement from a standalone client window. `GDK_DEBUG=no-portals` prevents unrelated portal activation, which the native test independently checks. Final paired runs have no accessibility/registry warnings; Xvfb retains the ordinary Mesa DRI3 warning. All content is synthetic; no microphone, provider, host clipboard, host input or installed app is used. The target example is a development peer and must not be shipped.

The primary owner is `captured_focus_selection_mutation_and_disclosure_match_real_released_transport` in `text_target.rs`, explicitly executed with `--ignored`. It protects real accessibility transport, independently observed widget edits and the disclosure boundary; the existing delivery tests separately own helper/receipt ordering. Its peer/monitor client support is now shared with the real Firefox composition. A repeated own-focus run exposed a timing-sensitive first-cache advertisement despite application registration; preparing/hiding the real client window before the first libatspi query and reusing it removes that warning without changing the thirty frozen outcomes. The final repeated GTK evidence is under `tmp/native-text-target-cache-ready.log`. This corpus does not call the complete application's recording/preview/retry controller or the clipboard/keyboard delivery pipeline. Source restoration can return false after focus moves while a separately invoked direct-edit method still succeeds; that does not authorize a controller to bypass restoration.

Actual Firefox UTF-16/keyboard insertion, Chromium and editor targets, isolated Wayland/terminal clipboard insertion, malformed/ambiguous accessibility trees, the 20,000-node guard, events racing initial discovery, non-UTF-8 executable paths and complete controller integration remain pending. The implementations preserve these rules, but this GTK corpus cannot prove those separate boundaries. All complete-workflow acceptance rows remain pending, the installed app/widget remain 1.6.0 and no whole-app performance claim is made.
